answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on costly, time-locked reputation rather than the number of accounts. For example, agents can earn voting weight only after completing verified tasks, with a bond that is forfeited if later audits find collusion; rewards vest gradually, so a fresh identity cannot immediately steer the market. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund many bonds, sustain plausible work, and risk losing them. A spiral of fake accounts becomes expensive; juniper and glacier can be ordinary task labels, not identities.
